rounding: RN64 denotes separately rounded IEEE binary64 nearest/ties-even; FCVTZS is signed64 truncation. Defensive C rejects nonnearest/unsupported FP state, invalid inputs and unsafe bounds.

admission: One selected stable direct MAudioEvent and one no-fade normal remainder; no neighbor-derived crossfades, explicit fade extents, loop/priority splitting or alternate selected stream.
Effective automatic fades disabled by the separately source-backed settings/ownership findings; absence of event fade pointers alone is insufficient.
Actual selected source stream and audible-state constraints come from prior studies. The helper neither executes nor proves source rendering.
Zero caller post-builder shift for the app operation; rate explicitly supplied by reconstruction context. Host resource and replaceable callbacks remain external state.

candidate_domain.coordinates: Finite normal-or-zero values within +/-86400; event/window endpoints ordered. Empty intersections and snapped-empty intervals are explicit dispositions.
candidate_domain.rate: Integral8k..192k; actual native rate getter permits a broader unvalidated runtime value.
candidate_domain.floating_point: arm64 FE_TONEAREST, FZ/DN/AH/FIZ off; no nonzero subnormal intermediates. Explicit volatile steps and FP_CONTRACT OFF.
candidate_domain.defensive_difference: Errors preserve caller output; empty unused fields are zero by wrapper convention. Native allocations/side effects are not claimed transactional.
candidate_domain.memory: All inputs by value, one caller output record, no target object lifetime or arbitrary callback behavior modeled.

limits: Raw REA slices omit imports/globals/vtables and surrounding routines; independent original-byte bindings supply only listed context.
Not a full ordinary host playback implementation, project mixer, effects, automation, multi-event overlap, loops, routing or device schedule.
The canonical source semantics depend on separate placed-event-context and prior timebase evidence; app source gates may conservatively exclude native cases.
